source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Intrusion symptoms, which center on recurrent unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or intense reactions to trauma reminders.","B":"Avoidance symptoms, which center on efforts to avoid trauma-related thoughts, feelings, people, places, or other reminders.","C":"Arousal and reactivity symptoms, including exaggerated startle, feeling on guard or on edge, irritability, and sleep difficulty.","D":"Negative cognition and mood symptoms, which include persistent negative beliefs, blame, emotional numbing, and loss of interest."}}
source_row.rationale: VA PTSD guidance places exaggerated startle, hypervigilance or feeling on guard, irritability, and sleep disturbance in the arousal-and-reactivity cluster. Option C is correct. Option A describes intrusion symptoms such as unwanted memories, nightmares, and flashbacks. Option B describes avoidance of trauma-related thoughts or reminders. Option D describes negative changes in beliefs, mood, interest, or connectedness rather than heightened arousal.
source_row.source_detail: VA National Center for PTSD — PTSD and DSM-5, Criterion E: Alterations in arousal and reactivity; includes hypervigilance/being on guard, exaggerated startle response, concentration problems, and sleep disturbance. VA notes DSM-5-TR did not change adult PTSD diagnostic criteria. Current VA National Center for PTSD professional guidance; DSM-5-TR adult PTSD criteria current; live source rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, behavioral adaptation and culturally/person-centered psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A client with post-traumatic stress disorder reports being easily startled, feeling constantly on guard, and having difficulty falling and staying asleep. Which PTSD symptom cluster do these findings represent?
